doc.title: Joe Temperley interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997

title: Stage riffs at the Jerome party and closing
summary: Talk about spontaneous background riffs on stage, with Conte Candoli and Norris Turney, then final thanks.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: I’m just fascinated by watching the interaction that goes on stage, especially when you’re doing, in the middle of a tune, and someone’s soloing, and one of the horn players will start a background riff. Like last night, I can’t even remember what set it was, but someone set up a two bar riff and the second time the riff came around everybody had it.
There’s no like fumbling or trying to hear. It’s almost like it was rehearsed but I don’t think it was.

Oh no. But I mean there’s a lot of patterns that you can play. And like for instance Conte Candoli came up with a great one last night and we just started — Dan Barrett and I just jumped on it right away, and it made it sound so good. And all he said was “Woody Herman,” you know?
I wrote a riff down I heard last night. It was like [scats].
Oh that’s Norris that does all those kind of things. Norris Turney, yeah. He does all those kind of riffs, yeah.
Well it’s fun to watch as well as listen.
Well good luck to you, and thanks for your time today.
Thank you very much. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -15-
